report.source_text: The patient underwent markedly rapid cognitive decline, and by day 7 since admission, episodes of severe agitations, akinetic mutism, aphasia, echolalia and echopraxia, and stiffness of limbs with upper limb myoclonic jerks were observed. Rowland Universal Dementia Assessment Scale (RUDAS) test at this time scored 0, with many of the items unable to be assessed. He also demonstrated a rapid functional decline to the point of being bedbound and incontinent of bowel and urine. He developed loss of swallowing function, therefore requiring nasogastric (NG) feeding.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with sudden-onset motor, functional, and cognitive decline including confusion, slurring of speech, dysgraphia, ataxic gait, and left-sided visual neglect. Initial suspicion was stroke. Brain MRI on day 1 postadmission showed no stroke but bilateral cortical ribboning on DWI and FLAIR, suggestive of sCJD (E005). Rapid clinical progression by day 7 included severe agitation, akinetic mutism, aphasia, echolalia, echopraxia, limb stiffness, and upper limb myoclonic jerks, with severe cognitive and functional decline (E002). EEG on day 6 showed diffuse encephalopathy without periodic sharp wave complexes typical of CJD (E007). Repeat MRI on day 10 showed no interval change despite clinical deterioration (E008). Brain autopsy was performed (ordered but no report available). Postmortem brain autopsy was positive for CJD, confirming diagnosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial brain MRI showed bilateral cortical ribboning on DWI and FLAIR suggestive of sCJD.
Rapid clinical deterioration by day 7 with myoclonic jerks, akinetic mutism, aphasia, and severe cognitive decline.
EEG revealed diffuse encephalopathy but no periodic sharp wave complexes typical for CJD.
Repeat MRI on day 10 showed no interval change despite worsening clinical symptoms.
Postmortem brain autopsy was positive for CJD confirming the diagnosis.
